query: What in an incident's description tends to signal it's a hardware problem?

per_column.name: affected_system_domain
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents into system domains (hardware_device, software_application, database, network) is directly central to the query about hardware signals, giving a clean grouping axis. Sample values are sound readings of the short_description (software installation -> software_application; MySQL connection -> database).

per_column.name: software_keyword_present
per_column.rationale: A bare boolean keyword flag is fairly generic and partly redundant with affected_system_domain; it offers limited independent leverage. However, as a complementary signal for isolating non-software (potentially hardware) incidents it retains some value. Values match the source text well.

per_column.name: description_action_type
per_column.rationale: Action-type categories (failure_malfunction, connectivity_issue, installation_request, etc.) provide a distinct behavioral axis that complements the domain column and can help distinguish hardware-typical failure/connectivity language. Sample values are well-grounded in the descriptions; NULL for unclear rows is acceptable.

judge.rationale: Two of the three columns (affected_system_domain, description_action_type) provide genuine, distinct grouping axes that directly serve the hardware-signal query, and all values are well-grounded in the short_description text with no observed hallucination. The software_keyword_present flag is more generic and partially redundant, lowering the holistic usefulness slightly but not the groundedness.
